note: Codes are the deposit's own column names (data/yoshimura_2026_psych_safety.py melts es1m1..es1m8 unchanged). The deposit carries no item text: the S1 Codebook labels them only 'Emotional support item 1..8'; the paper prints one ES example ('He/she encourages me when I am feeling down at work'). Paper cites the scale to Komaki & Tanaka 1993 and Komaki 1994 [18,19]; Komaki 1994's Appendix prints the 14-item scale, emotional support items 1-8 and instrumental items 9-14, matching this deposit's es1m1-8 / isu1m9-14 numbering, and its item 1 is the Japanese of the paper's English example. item_text = Komaki's Appendix items 1-8, transcribed by reading the page image (the PDF text layer is garbled OCR) - a human spot-check of the Japanese is advisable. Yoshimura's administered Japanese is not in the deposit or supplements, so the wording is the canonical 1994 text; the study administered it about the supervisor only and may have adapted stems. Alignment of es1m<k> to Komaki item k is inferred from that numbering (paper_order). Translation: item 1 English is the study's own (paper Methods 2.3.2); items 2-8 English machine-translated by this project. option_text is the English 1-5 anchors from the study's S1 Codebook (strongly disagree..strongly agree); the administered Japanese anchors are not published (Komaki 1994 only states 5 steps from 'sou omou' to 'sou omowanai'), so option_text is English with option_text_translated blank. instructions left blank (none published). Rights: no register row; J-STAGE page shows only '(c) 1994 Japanese Association of Health Psychology' - a bare article copyright notice, no reservation of any right on the scale located, so not a block. Step 3b: no mismatch - table is the supervisor emotional support scale; dictionary Description 'ES scale (unlabeled)' could be improved to 'supervisor emotional support (Komaki 1994), 8 items'. Verification PARTIAL: parcels {1,2,5},{3,6,7},{4,8} (S1 File) reproduce S1 Table B exactly; {6,7,8} (Komaki's three evaluation items) is the top of 56 triplets.
public_note: Item wording is the published 1994 Japanese scale (Komaki) that the study cites, not a copy of the study's own questionnaire, which was not released; English for items 2-8 was translated by IRW, and the response labels are the study's English codebook anchors rather than the Japanese wording respondents saw
